Folks — forwarding MedKit's ask. TL;DR: pilot surged to ~80 seats for three days (they included usage). They are asking for a one-time seat-swap and a retro credit to offset overage charges.

Why this matters: MedKit is in a time-boxed pilot with a clear path to a committed deployment; losing momentum here risks the whole deal (Deal DK-2026-1147). They are asking to resolve before their exec review on 6/15.

Attachments: medkit_pilot_usage_202606.xlsx, signed-moa-2026-05-10.pdf

Proposed ask to finance: provide a retro credit capped at the 75-seat equivalent for the surge days and allow seat-swap (credit applied against pilot invoice). Estimated impact: ~$9k revenue reduction this month but preserves deal.

Can finance/ops expedite? Jordan, Kimberley — can you weigh in on approvals needed for a one-time concession? Marissa, can you sign off if numbers check?

Thanks,
Dylan

Thanks for the context. I pulled the usage file and ran a quick calc. If we cap the credit to 75 seats for the three surge days and apply the pilot discounted rate, the gross credit is about $8,700. Net impact after amortized onboarding incentives would be ~ $7,400.

Questions/notes:
- Is MedKit asking for a permanent seat reallocation or just a one-time accounting credit + swap for the pilot invoice? Please confirm language; permanent changes require contract amendment.
- We should require a written acknowledgement that Redwood's approval is a one-time concession conditioned on them signing a 12-month commitment by 7/15.
- Finance needs the approved memo and a VP/CFO signature for any credit > $5k per policy.

I attached a short proposed credit memo (proposed_credit_calc.pdf) and redlines to the suggested acknowledgement clause. If Jordan and Dylan confirm the commitment trigger, I can route to Marissa for signoff.

Kimberly
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

To be explicit to MedKit: we are proposing a one-time retro credit capped to 75-seat equivalent for the surge days and a seat-swap applied to this pilot invoice only. This is not a contract amendment. Condition: MedKit must commit to a 12-month paid deployment (minimum 250k ARR) and sign the commercial agreement by 2026-07-15. Ellen — please confirm you can commit to the sign-by date or propose an alternative deadline.

Proposed language for Marissa's memo:
"Redwood grants a one-time retroactive billing credit to MedKit AI not to exceed $8,700 gross (estimated $7,400 net after incentives). This concession is conditioned on MedKit's execution of a 12-month committed agreement with a minimum $250k ARR before July 15, 2026. The credit will be applied to the June pilot invoice. This approval is granted as a one-time commercial exception and does not change the terms of existing MOA."

If both finance and Marissa approve, I'll send the formal acknowledgement for Ellen to sign.

Dylan
